note: SH1043 — what the console costs to load, before the first row of content. Read by test/console-size-budget.test.mjs against a built ../shio-app/src/main/resources/public, and printed by `pnpm --filter shio-react run size`. Raise a ceiling deliberately and say why in the commit, the way token-budgets.properties has governed the agent's cost since SH113: this is the same rule for the half of the product a person waits for.
seed: SH1043 seeded this at 7473483 raw / 2200187 gzip, and SH1044 spent that number the same day: deleting vite.config.ts's `manualChunks` took it to 1542579 raw / 413169 gzip, because the rule written to keep GraphiQL out of the eager bundle was what put it there. Four entries went with it — vendor-graphiql.js, vendor-graphiql.css, vendor-codemirror.js and vendor-lib.js are no longer eager, and this gate fails on a ceiling that outlives its chunk, which is how they came to be deleted here rather than left as numbers nobody was measuring. The ceilings carry ~5% of room for the reason SH736 gives one gate over: a ceiling set to the measurement refuses the next change instead of measuring it.
raised: SH1046 raised the eager ceilings and index.js's, and the reason is the whole of what this file is for: adopting `@tanstack/react-query` cost 32894 raw / 10054 gzip, measured here before and after, against seventeen catalogue reads that each refetched a whole collection on every mount. That is the trade this gate exists to make visible — 2.4% of the gzipped load for a folder-to-folder walk that stops refetching the post-type catalogue per folder. Nothing else moved: index.css, breadcrumb.context.js and rolldown-runtime.js are byte-identical across the change. SH1056 raised the two eager ceilings again, by 7000 raw / 2000 gzip: the site editor's Languages section, the translations menu's narrowing and the rules both read cost 6871 raw / 1854 gzip, all of it index.js, measured by building the tree with and without them (1583519 → 1590390 raw, 425245 → 427099 gzip). That took the raw room to 3.9% of the ceiling, under the 4% the headroom check asks for; the raise restores it without touching index.js's own ceiling, which still has 44 KB under it. SH1060 raised them again, by 6000 raw / 2000 gzip: SH1058's out-of-date marker in the translations menu and SH1060's Languages board cost 5873 raw / 1349 gzip together, measured on the same build before and after (1590390 → 1596263 raw, 427099 → 428448 gzip). The board is a screen a curator opens when a site has more than one language, and it is the first console surface that turns the translation backlog into a work list; index.js's own ceiling is untouched and still has 37 KB under it. SH1061's side-by-side workspace measured 4326 raw / 950 gzip on top of that (1596263 → 1600589 raw), and the raw ceiling went 1668000 -> 1674000 with it: at 1668000 the fit was 700 bytes, which is a ceiling that refuses the next addition rather than measuring it — SH736's lesson, and the reason every raise here leaves room. SH1065 raised the gzip ceiling alone, 449000 -> 452000, and the reason is the headroom rule rather than a feature: reading the server's own Content-Disposition on the site download — so a zip saved from the console and one written by `shio export` are the same file instead of two names for one artifact — measured under 100 gzip bytes (1568.0 -> 1568.1 KB raw, 420.9 KB gzip on both builds), and it was those bytes that took the room from 18,010 to 17,950 against the 17,960 the 4% check asks for. A raise of 3000 puts the room back to 4.6% rather than to the measurement, which is the same lesson every entry above records: a ceiling at the total refuses the next change instead of measuring it. The raw ceiling is untouched and still has 106 KB under it, which is why only one of the two moved. SH1088 raised nothing: taking design system 2026.3.12 moved the eager total from 1568.1 to 1570.3 KB raw and 420.9 to 423.0 KB gzip, inside both ceilings, but regrouped the chunks. breadcrumb.context.js is no longer emitted, and index.es.js (397.6 KB raw, 126.4 KB gzip) carries the package's ES entry with the React runtime it shares, while index.js fell to 924 KB. The entry was renamed to the chunk that now exists, with ~5% room. The +2.2 KB raw left the eager raw room at 66,013 bytes against the 66,960 the 4% check asks for, so the raw ceiling went 1674000 -> 1680000 (4.3% room), for the same reason SH1065 moved the gzip one: a ceiling at the total refuses the next change instead of measuring it. The gzip ceiling did not move. SH964 raised the eager raw ceiling 1680000 -> 1700000, the eager gzip ceiling 452000 -> 460000 and index.es.js to 443000 raw / 141000 gzip: mounting VigletAssistant as the status dock cost 14.6 KB raw / 5.3 KB gzip, all of it index.es.js, measured by building with and without it (eager 1572.0 -> 1586.6 KB raw, 423.6 -> 429.0 KB gzip; index.es.js 397.6 -> 411.9 KB raw). Loading it with lazy() was measured too and saved nothing: the bundler keeps the design system's whole ES entry in one shared eager chunk, so the component lands there whichever way it is imported. The raises restore ~4.4% of room on both totals and ~5% on the chunk. SH969 raised the eager raw ceiling 1700000 -> 1712000 for the headroom rule rather than one feature: the dock work after SH964's raise (SH966's report store and refusal reporter, SH968's run tracker and shared stream, SH969's schedule reports and replay) took the eager load from 1586.6 to 1594.0 KB raw, leaving 66.2 KB of room against the 68 KB the 4% check asks for. The new ceiling leaves 4.7%. The same work took the eager gzip total to 431.7 KB against 449.2 KB, 3.9% of room, so the gzip ceiling went 460000 -> 466000 (5.1%). Every chunk ceiling is untouched. SH988 raised the eager raw ceiling 1712000 -> 1724000 for the headroom rule: SH971's dock preferences dialog, SH972's editor dock and SH988's version rail, diff and inline review diff took the eager load from 1594.0 to 1606.4 KB raw, leaving 65.5 KB of room against the 66.9 KB the 4% check asks for. The new ceiling leaves 4.7%; the gzip ceiling and every chunk ceiling are untouched.

index.js.why: the console itself plus the shared vendor code the bundler folded in once `manualChunks` stopped hand-placing it: React, the router, the query layer (SH1046) and the libraries every route needs

index.css.why: Tailwind's output plus the design system's own sheet

index.es.js.why: the design system's ES entry and the React runtime it shares with the console, which the bundler emits as one eager chunk since 2026.3.11 (SH1088); it replaced breadcrumb.context.js, and index.js shrank by what it took

rolldown-runtime.js.why: the bundler's own module runtime, which every other chunk is loaded through
